$$\begin{aligned} y &= 2x + 9 \\ 3x + 5y &= 19 \end{aligned}$$

The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $y$?

distractorNotes.A: A sign error: the size is right but the sign is wrong.
distractorNotes.B: This is the value of $x$, not $y$.
distractorNotes.C: An arithmetic slip: redo the last computation carefully.

medium:mcq:1.stem:
$$\begin{aligned} 5x + y &= -1 \\ 6x + 6y &= 18 \end{aligned}$$

The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $y$?

distractorNotes.A: The wrong sign was used for $x$ when substituting back.
distractorNotes.B: A sign error: the size is right but the sign is wrong.
distractorNotes.C: This is the value of $x$, not $y$.

solution: To eliminate $y$, multiply the first equation by $6$ and the second equation by $1$: $$\begin{aligned} 30x + 6y &= -6 \\ 6x + 6y &= 18 \end{aligned}$$
Subtract the second new equation from the first: $24x = -24$.
Substitute $x = -1$ into the first equation: $y - 5 = -1$, so $y = 4$.

medium:mcq:2.stem:
$$\begin{aligned} x + 6y &= 10 \\ 2x - 5y &= 3 \end{aligned}$$

The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $y$?

distractorNotes.A: A sign error: the size is right but the sign is wrong.
distractorNotes.C: The wrong sign was used for $x$ when substituting back.
distractorNotes.D: This is the value of $x$, not $y$.

solution: To eliminate $y$, multiply the first equation by $-5$ and the second equation by $6$: $$\begin{aligned} -5x - 30y &= -50 \\ 12x - 30y &= 18 \end{aligned}$$
Subtract the second new equation from the first: $-17x = -68$.
Substitute $x = 4$ into the first equation: $6y + 4 = 10$, so $y = 1$.

medium:mcq:3.stem:
$$\begin{aligned} 4x - 3y &= -10 \\ -2x + y &= 4 \end{aligned}$$

The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $y$?

distractorNotes.A: A sign error: the size is right but the sign is wrong.
distractorNotes.B: This is the value of $x$, not $y$.
distractorNotes.D: The wrong sign was used for $x$ when substituting back.

solution: To eliminate $y$, multiply the first equation by $1$ and the second equation by $-3$: $$\begin{aligned} 4x - 3y &= -10 \\ 6x - 3y &= -12 \end{aligned}$$
Subtract the second new equation from the first: $-2x = 2$.
Substitute $x = -1$ into the first equation: $-3y - 4 = -10$, so $y = 2$.

solution: The $y$-terms are opposites, so add the equations: $6x = -42$.

hard:mcq:1.stem:
$$\begin{aligned} 7x + y &= 29 \\ x + 7y &= -13 \end{aligned}$$

The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $x - y$?

distractorNotes.B: This is the value of $x$ alone.
distractorNotes.C: Divided by the wrong coefficient after combining the equations.

solution: The coefficients of $x$ and $y$ trade places between the equations, so subtract the second equation from the first: $6x - 6y = 42$.
You never need $x$ and $y$ on their own. They are $x = \frac{9}{2}$ and $y = -\frac{5}{2}$, which take longer to find.
